mathematics.assertion_tested: Lean kernel acceptance of compatible integer polynomial solution towers for every compatible exact integer parameter path under only initial actual solved-Jacobian surjectivity; construction of such paths for every prescribed p-adic parameter target in the base ball; actual p-adic root endpoints with exact free coordinates and retained tower precisions; exactly p^(m-e) actual prescribed residue lifts for each next parameter digit; square solved-block uniqueness; inherited prescribed obstructions, lifting, chart, and root-motion theorems; expanded statement contracts and mathematically invalid controls
mathematics.coefficient_domain: Finite rectangular systems of integer polynomials in m solved and k parameter variables, e equations, positive modulus q, depth L>=1, actual lower root x, actual solved-coordinate Jacobian modulo q surjective. Exact integer towers include composite q and q=1; p-adic completion and count p^(m-e) require prime p. Uniqueness requires m=e
mathematics.conventions: A supplied integer parameter path starts exactly at x_free and its nth increment is divisible by q^(L+n). The constructed full tower starts exactly at x, has exactly those integer free coordinates, is a polynomial root to depth L+n and retains the initial actual solved Jacobian. For an arbitrary p-adic target tau congruent to x_free modulo p^L, both parameter path and full tower are constructed. The endpoint is an exact root with free part tau and is congruent to tower level n modulo p^(L+n). Prescribed branching counts actual residue classes, not integer representatives
